text:
sam: heads-up, rack-18 (edge-usw1) is showing NVLink saturation that correlates with multi-tenant tail-latency spikes. Not CPU or PCIe, nvlink counters look hot.

mira: can you paste the counters?

sam: sure — grabbing snapshot now:

```
nvlink_counters rack-18/shelf3/node7
links_active=4, bw_avg=78GB/s, bw_95p=95GB/s, retries=120, link_errors=3
per_gpu_txq_depth=[128,130,127,129], hbm_util=[82,85,84,83]
```

sam: spikes start ~11:04 UTC, coincides with two large tenant batch jobs + a few realtime slices.

lee: oof. sounds like NVLink oversubscribe between MIG partitions and host-batched workloads. Any tenant ids?

sam: tenant_a (background batch), tenant_b (dedicated small pool but colocated on same shelf), tenant_c (realtime).

toya: is this transient or recurring?

sam: recurring every 6-8 hours, usually after warmup windows when batch jobs backfill. Pattern is consistent for last 3 days.

mira: quick mitigation options: 1) move tenant_b out of rack-18 to another rack (warm fallback), 2) temporarily denylist batch jobs from rack-18, 3) preemptively shepherd real-time slices to dedicated hotlane. Which is least disruptive?

jordan: denylist + shepherd seems safest short-term. Moving dedicated pools is heavy and requires re-provisioning.

lee: agree. denylist code lives in allocator service. We can add an NVLINK_HIGH signal to the policy and short-circuit batch placement.

sam: also want a chargeback/telemetry note — tenant_b was on a cheaper dedicated carve that lets them pack more. We should flag cost-vs-isolation tradeoffs.

mira: opened quick PR to add signal: alloc/signal_nvlink_high.ops -> will short-circuit batch placement to low-cost pools. Pushing canary in 10m.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for branch "nvlink-shepherd-canary" — CI job queued.

sre-ci: running integration canary against uswest-edge staging. Will run traffic with tenant_c realtime load + synthetic batch to validate rollback triggers.

toya: what's the rollback rule?

lee: rollback if 95p latency for realtime increases by >10% or alloc failures spike >0.5% for 5m. Also auto-unlist after 30m if no improvement.

mira: adding a temporary denylist config:
```
config: {
  "signal": "nvlink_high",
  "action": "denylist_batch",
  "duration_sec": 1800,
  "min_impact_samples": 3
}
```

sam: thanks. can we also emit a metric tenant_nvlink_collision{tenant, rack} so billing/product can follow up?

jordan: yes — create metric and tag with "isolation_candidate" when tenant has >threshold noisy events in 24h.

mira: quick canary results: after denylist flip (11:19 UTC) realtime p95 dropped from 210ms -> 120ms on rack-18. Batch throughput slightly affected (-6%). ops-bot: annotate. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: annotation added to incident stream with link: https://ops.example.internal/incident/1778881112/nvlink-shepherding

sam: good. To follow: 1) propose permanent policy (denylist threshold + chargeback flag) 2) run a 24h trial to see false positives 3) surface tenants that repeatedly cause collisions to sales/CS for isolation upsell.

lee: working on allocator PR to make signal pluggable. Will include tests and a runtime flag for auto-unlist durations.

toya: can infra team triage which racks have hardware NVLink mismatch versions? mismatch can exacerbate contention.

sam: noted — inventory shows rack-18 has one node on older NVLINK gen (fw v1.2) while others are v1.4. I'll attach a CSV.

mira: long-term options: stronger rack-level isolation, smaller fractional dedicated carveouts, or network-level QoS for NVLink-flows (harder). Need tradeoff doc.

jordan: I'll draft a short tradeoff doc and include cost delta for moving tenant_b to a non-shared dedicated slice vs current pack.

sam: action owners: lee (allocator change), mira (run 24h trial + metrics), jordan (tradeoff doc & CS contact), toya (inventory audit). Re-check tomorrow EOD.

mira: thanks everyone — nice win for shepherding. :sparkles:

lee: can we add a permanent alert on nvlink retries > 50 in 5m for a rack? That would've flagged earlier.

sre-ci: adding alert proposal to pager-duty playbook: nvlink_retry_rate_high -> P2 page.

sam: perfect. closing thread after EOD followups.
